summary: The Marshall Islands lets US, Palauan and Micronesian citizens enter without a visa or time limit, waives visas for up to 90 days for EU and UK citizens, Taiwan and Guatemala, gives a free 90-day visa on arrival to citizens of the many countries it has diplomatic relations with, and requires everyone else to obtain a USD 100 visitor visa before travelling.

tips.text: US citizens are visa-exempt under the Compact of Free Association, with no restriction on the period of stay. The RMI Division of Immigration says the Compact exempts them from entry visa requirements only: work registration is still required. Under the Compact, it says, Marshallese citizens may live and work in the United States.

The UK government says medical facilities are very limited, and advises bringing sufficient prescription medicines and comprehensive travel insurance covering all medical costs, including medical evacuation.
Australia's Smartraveller says ATMs are not available at the airport and that the departure fee must be paid in US dollars cash.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for the Marshall Islands?
faq.answer: US citizens do not: the Division of Immigration lists them as visa-exempt under the Compact of Free Association, with no restriction on the period of stay, as are citizens of Palau and the Federated States of Micronesia. EU and UK citizens, Taiwan and Guatemala get a free visa waiver for up to 90 days; citizens of countries with diplomatic relations with the Marshall Islands — including Australia, New Zealand, Canada, Japan and South Korea — get a free visa on arrival for up to 90 days. Everyone else must obtain a USD 100 Visitor's Visa from the Division of Immigration before travelling.

faq.question: How does the visa on arrival work?
faq.answer: It is granted on arrival, free of charge, to citizens of countries on the Division of Immigration's visa-on-arrival list. You need a passport valid 6 months beyond your departure, a confirmed return or onward ticket, any visa you need for your next destination, and sufficient funds. It allows up to 90 days and cannot be extended.

faq.question: How long can I stay in the Marshall Islands?
faq.answer: Up to 90 days under the visa waiver or the visa on arrival; neither can be extended, changing status and working are not permitted, and studying is excluded for visa-on-arrival holders and for Taiwanese and Guatemalan passport holders. US citizens under the Compact, and citizens of Palau and the Federated States of Micronesia, have no time limit at all.

faq.question: Can Americans work in the Marshall Islands under the Compact?
faq.answer: Not on the Compact alone. The RMI Division of Immigration says the Compact exempts US citizens from entry visa requirements only, and that work registration is still required.

faq.question: Is travel insurance mandatory?
faq.answer: No official source we could read makes travel insurance a condition of entry. The UK government advises comprehensive insurance covering all medical costs, including medical evacuation, because medical facilities are very limited.
